repaired.name: Scenario
repaired.script:
triggered := false
if (triggered == true) {
wait until((#Main_Window).windowCovering_currentPosition <= 0)
triggered = false
}
wait until((#Main_Window).windowCovering_currentPosition > 0)
all(#Speaker).speaker_speak("The window is open")
triggered = true

diagnosis.summary: The IR implements a rising-edge wait followed by an action. The candidate polls the condition at the start of the body (line 2) and only acts if the flag is false (line 3). Evidence F2 shows the condition became true at t=100ms, but the candidate emitted no action because the `if` guard on line 3 was false (triggered was already true from a previous iteration or the logic flow prevented entry). The IR requires blocking on the rising edge, not sampling it periodically.
diagnosis.change_summary: Replaced the periodic polling `if` with the required rising-edge state machine: block until the condition is false (rearm), then block until it becomes true, perform the action, and set the flag. This ensures the action fires exactly when the edge occurs, regardless of the wrapper period.
